newsitem.title: USA: Versace service set; new murder seen as unrelated.
newsitem.headline: Versace service set; new murder seen as unrelated.

text.p: Friends and fans of slain fashion designer Gianni Versace were to remember him on Friday at a church service in the glamorous Miami Beach area he personified as his suspected killer eluded a vast manhunt.

Police and FBI agents probing Versace's murder rushed to the scene of the killing of a Miami doctor on Thursday. But after searching the house and nearby woods they said no link had been established despite speculation that the Italian designer's suspected assassin had struck again.
Andrew Cunanan, the alleged "spree killer" and homosexual prostitute suspected of gunning down Versace outside his Miami Beach mansion on Tuesday, remained at large, armed and dangerous, police said.

"We have been receiving tips he is in south Florida. All are being investigated," Paige Patterson of the Florida Department of Law Enforcement said. "There have been some real positive tips, but obviously he has not been arrested yet."
Cunanan is the only suspect in the murder of Versace, 50, a leading light of the international fashion scene who dressed the rich and beautiful.
Cunanan, 27, described as a gregarious, charming male prostitute who lived off wealthy, older gay patrons, is also wanted for four other murders.

Versace's body was cremated at a Fort Lauderdale funeral home, staff said. His sister, Donatella, and other family members left Miami on a charter plane on Thursday night with his ashes for a funeral in Italy, witnesses said.
Hundreds of friends and admirers as well as Miami dignitaries were expected to attend a memorial service for him at St. Patrick's Church in Miami Beach on Friday.

Versace, a homosexual, was a prominent resident of Miami Beach, a trendy area of night clubs, cafes, model agencies and Art Deco hotels popular with fun seekers from around the world and home to a large gay community.
He was shot twice in the head on the steps of his Spanish-style mansion on Ocean Drive as he strolled home from a cafe after picking up magazines.
Dade County Mayor Alex Penelas, Miami Beach Mayor Seymour Gelber and Italian Consul General Gian Campagnola were due to give eulogies at the service.

The family asked for donations to be sent to two of Versace's favourite charities in lieu of flowers -- the Elton John Aids Foundation and the Sting Rainforest Foundation. Both rock stars are among the firmament of luminaries he dressed.
The hunt for Cunanan led law officers to the Miami Springs suburb after a Silvio Alfonso, a 44-year-old doctor, was found murdered in his bedroom on Thursday morning.
A man matching Cunanan's description was reported to have been seen leaving the house, but police later played down the incident, saying many men in Miami matched his looks.
A search with tracker dogs through nearby woods as police helicopters hovered overhead was called off after no clues or suspects were found, police spokesman Juan Castillo said.
"At this time there is no link. But we haven't ruled out anything," Castillo told Reuters on Thursday evening.
Local television quoted neighbours as saying Alfonso was homosexual, but others said he had a wife and children in Cuba.
FBI agents have been hunting Cunanan across the United States in connection with the murders of four other men, including his homosexual lover.

Chicago police said on Thursday they had an arrest warrant for Cunanan for the murder of Chicago real estate tycoon Lee Miglin, 72, a police spokesman said. Federal prosecutors in New Jersey on Wednesday formally charged Cunanan with the May 9 shooting death of William Reese, a caretaker at a national cemetery in Pennsville, New Jersey.
Police found a red pickup he allegedly stole from Reese in a Miami Beach garage.
Police say they do not know if Versace had any relationship with Cunanan, although Vanity Fair writer Maureen Orth said the two men had met at least once in San Francisco.
Police have distributed posters of Cunanan throughout south Florida and warned gays in particular to be alert.
